lesson.text: Quick memory: how many seconds of rubbing make hands clean? (20.) Today: measuring, cutting and cooking safely.
Scales first show zero with the bowl on: then spoon slowly to the amount. A measuring cup has marks: a quarter, a half, three quarters.
Slice with the claw grip: fingertips tucked in like a claw, the knife going up and down slowly. Use a child-safe knife with a grown-up.
At the hob a grown-up is always with you. Turn pan handles in, away from the edge, use a low heat, and never leave cooking alone.
A hob stays hot after it is off: the hot light shows it. Keep hands away until the light goes off.
Try it in the world: open the practice kitchen and cook with the scales, the cup, the claw and the hob.

exercises.explain: Zero with the bowl on, so only the food is weighed.

exercises.prompt: A grown-up is with you at the hob.
exercises.explain: True: always a grown-up at the hob.

exercises.prompt: Which grip keeps fingers safe when slicing?
The hob is off, so it is cool at once.
exercises.explain: False: it stays hot for a while; the hot light shows it.

exercises.prompt: Three quarters of a cup is...
Weighing flour: put it in order.
exercises.explain: Bowl on, zero, spoon slowly, stop at the amount.

exercises.prompt: Safe at the hob or not?
exercises.explain: Handles in and a low heat are safe; leaving it and touching it are not.

exercises.prompt: 200 g of flour, then 50 g more. How much?
Never leave cooking alone on the hob.
exercises.hint: Things can boil over or burn.
